witness.note: sidon_max[N-1] is the asserted maximum size of a Sidon subset of {1..N} (pairwise sums a_i+a_j with i<=j all distinct), for N=1..8, verified exhaustively in both directions. The universal asymptotic branch of the canonical statement is NOT covered (no finite-reduction theorem exists) and is excluded, exactly as L1 states.

claim: verify(witness) returns True (and only True; every failed check raises) exactly when, for every N<=8, the maximum size of a Sidon subset of {1..N} is [1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4] (both existence and impossibility halves, by exhaustive enumeration over all 2^N subsets with exact integer arithmetic), and for r in {2,3} the minimal value of sum_{n<=N} f_r(n)^2 subject to the finite basis constraint [r,N] subset of rA is computed exactly over all subsets of {1..N}, satisfies the provable lower bound N-r+1 and monotonicity in N, with each exhibited minimizer independently re-verified. Repair note: the previous submission's extra hand-derived ceiling invariant K[5]==K[6]==K[7] was mathematically wrong (k(7)=4 via {1,2,5,7}); it has been removed — the exhaustive enumeration alone determines every entry, so no hand argument is load-bearing. covers="fragment": the universal asymptotic branch (existence, for every r>=2, of an infinite basis of order r with O(x) square-sum) has no finite-reduction theorem and remains uncertifiable, exactly as recorded in L1.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
